dedupe_keys.name: cloud outage tracker 2026 axis intelligence operator postmortem log of major cloud incidents

description: The Cloud Outage Tracker logs major public-cloud and core-internet-infrastructure outages for which the operator has published its own post-incident document. Contents: nine incidents at the 9 August 2026 update, spanning AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Cloudflare and DENIC, six of which carry a computed Diagnostic Lag Ratio (the share of customer impact time before the operator knew what had broken) with a mean of 0.27 and a median of 0.10. Examples on the page: Microsoft's West US network outage of 23 July 2026, where engineers correlated the anomaly 2 hours 35 minutes after impact began, and a Google europe-west4-a incident on 15 July 2026 in which hall temperatures reached 44 degrees Celsius after a voltage drop cascaded into a cooling failure, causing a 14 hour 55 minute interruption. Producer: Axis Intelligence Research, updated weekly; the inclusion rules require an operator-published document stating at least start time and cause. Coverage: global, five providers. Access: a public page with a free CSV download. Licence and cost: free; the tracker page states CC BY 4.0 for the CSV. Caveats: a small, curated commercial log with a self-defined metric, two entries flagged as not fully verified, and AWS entries only up to October 2025. Simulation uses: incident causes, durations and cascades inform data centre and cloud resilience scenarios. Related records: Azure status history (data-azure-status-history-post-incident-reviews) and the cloud uptime archive (data-cloud-uptime-archive).
